title: The startup heal finds no admin edit, so the code copy overwrites the stale July row
subtitle: A replay of today's fixed startup against the July row, following the real code and its test for a stale, never-edited row.

outcome.title: The model reads all 15 rules again
lines: The heal writes no archive row, so the next startup can heal again. Tutor replies still carry no prompt version; only lesson notes do.

captions.title: Register the code copy before reading anything
captions.text: The app records the key `ai-tutor-layer1`, its default text in code and the 8 `{{name}}` slots that code fills. Engineers review this copy in git.

captions.title: Load the database row into the cache
captions.text: The row has the old text, without rules 14 and 15. Each process keeps it in memory. Before the fix, startup ended here and the row won.

captions.title: Compare the cached text with the code copy
captions.text: If the two are equal, there is nothing to heal. Here they differ, so the app must decide which copy wins.

captions.title: Ask whether a person ever edited the row
captions.text: Every admin save first copies the old text into an archive table. 0 archived versions means no person changed it, so the code copy wins.

captions.title: Reset the row without writing an archive
captions.text: The heal writes the code copy over the row and reloads the cache. It writes no archive row, which would make the row look edited and stop later heals.

captions.title: Fill the slots and send the whole prompt on each turn
captions.text: A session reads the rules from the cache once. On every turn code computes the 8 slot values, and the filled text with all 15 rules goes to the model.

captions.title: Stamp the prompt version and model on the result
captions.text: Tutor replies carry no stamp today. The lesson-note writer saves prompt "v1" and the model id in two columns, so a bad note can be traced months later.
